verdicts.tldr: the only case named after indirectExclude cannot reach it, so a maintainer editing that list reads a false all-clear
verdicts.details: The case changes examples/gno.land/p/x/mid/v0/lib.gno, and the only importer of mid in fakeRepo is r/x/leaf (plan_test.go:36-37). The fixture realm the case is named for imports base, not mid (plan_test.go:42-43), so it is never in dependents() and the hasPrefixAny(p, indirectExclude) skip at plan.go:244 is evaluated once, for leaf, where the prefix gno.land/r/tests/ does not match. The rule is pinned only by the two cases named for something else, which is what the finder's deletion run shows. Fix: in fakeRepo, give gno.land/r/tests/vm/fixture the import "gno.land/p/x/mid/v0" so the case it is named for actually reaches the skip.
verdicts.evidence: plan_test.go:42-43 pkg("examples/gno.land/r/tests/vm/fixture", ..., "package fixture\nimport \"gno.land/p/x/base/v0\"\n"); plan.go:244 if !changedPkgs[p] && hasPrefixAny(p, indirectExclude). BFS from mid: rev["gno.land/p/x/mid/v0"] = [gno.land/r/x/leaf] only, so the fixture is never a candidate.
verdicts.verify_by: in a worktree at ecf7af0f2, set `var indirectExclude = []string{}` and run `cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestBuildPlan ./...`; read which subtests fail

verdicts.tldr: the quarantine case asserts nothing a quarantine rule owns: it exits on the same line as the docs-only case
verdicts.details: pkgRoot is examples/gno.land (plan.go:22) and LoadPkgs walks only that subtree (plan.go:109-110), so examples/quarantined/gno.land/r/x/quar is never loaded and never lands in byDir. The changed path then fails strings.HasPrefix(f, pkgRoot+"/") at plan.go:217 and takes the same continue as docs/x.md in `nothing relevant`. Deleting that prefix guard leaves the case green, because byDir[path.Dir(f)] is nil for a package LoadPkgs never walked; grep finds no quarantine concept in any .go file. Fix: drop the case, or make it a real assertion by having LoadPkgs walk examples/ whole and pinning that quarantined packages are excluded there.
verdicts.evidence: grep -rn 'quarantin' misc/gnopreview -> plan.go:20 (comment), README.md:24, plan_test.go:12/44/48/96 only; no code. plan.go:22 pkgRoot = examplesRel + "/gno.land"; plan.go:217 if !strings.HasPrefix(f, pkgRoot+"/") || !renderRelevant(f) { continue }.
verdicts.verify_by: grep plan.go for a quarantine check: `grep -n quarantin misc/gnopreview/*.go` returns only plan_test.go, and pkgRoot is examples/gno.land

verdicts.tldr: no directory page carries the link this rests on, so no realm gets the duplicate page the finding charges it with
verdicts.details: The named emitter is a prefix helper, not a link: DirLinkTypeSource.LinkPrefix returns pkgPath+"$source&file=" and its single caller concatenates a real file name onto it at view_directory.go:45, so every directory-listing href carries a value. The template's one hardcoded link is $source&file=README.md (directory.html:48), and the overview's two license links interpolate License.FileName, which overview_license.go sets only from a name matched by ReLicenseFileName and is therefore never empty. With no page emitting file= empty, the crawl never captures the URL, so the claimed one-unbudgeted-duplicate-per-dependency-realm cost does not occur. Fix: none needed for this claim; the uncharged-empty-value asymmetry itself is candidate 148.
verdicts.evidence: view_directory.go:41-48 `Link: linkType.LinkPrefix(pkgPath) + file` inside `for i, file := range files`; components/views/directory.html:48 `<a href="{{ $pkgpath }}$source&file=README.md">`; grep of components/views for a bare `file="` returns nothing.
verdicts.verify_by: cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run TestProbeEmptyFileValue -v . with the probe file; grep -n 'source&file=' ../../gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/components/view_directory.go for the emitting site

verdicts.tldr: the subtest named for the indirect-exclude rule stays green with that rule deleted, so its name promises coverage nothing holds
verdicts.details: fakeRepo's import graph is base <- mid <- leaf, with the fixture realm hanging off base (plan_test.go:33-43). A change to mid therefore yields dependents {mid, leaf}; the fixture is not reachable, so plan.go:244-246 never fires for this case whatever indirectExclude holds. What does pin the rule is `transitive dependency pulls both dependents`, which changes base and needs the fixture excluded from the result. Fix: repoint the fixture's import at gno.land/p/x/mid/v0 so the named case exercises the skip.
verdicts.evidence: plan_test.go:34-43: mid imports base; leaf imports mid; r/tests/vm/fixture imports base. plan.go:240-248 iterates dependents(pkgs, changedPkgs), and for seeds={gno.land/p/x/mid/v0} that set is {mid, leaf} only.
verdicts.verify_by: in a scratch worktree at ecf7af0: sed -i '244,246d' misc/gnopreview/plan.go && cd misc/gnopreview && go test -run 'TestBuildPlan/tests_fixtures_are_not_pulled_in_indirectly' ./... && go test -run TestBuildPlan ./...

verdicts.tldr: two fixture lines read as coverage that does not exist: a reader looking for the orphan-realm case finds its fixture and no assertion
verdicts.details: `lonely` appears once in the package, at plan_test.go:40, and in no test case; no wantRealms names it and no case changes it. examples/gnowork.toml is written at plan_test.go:26, but LoadPkgs walks examples/gno.land and never reads it; the only reader of that file is findRoot in main.go:295, which no test calls (the package has no main_test.go and BuildPlan takes root directly). Fix: drop both lines, or add the orphan-realm case the lonely fixture implies.
verdicts.evidence: grep -rn 'gnowork\|lonely' misc/gnopreview -> plan_test.go:26, plan_test.go:40, main.go:285/295/300, plan.go comments. ls misc/gnopreview/*_test.go -> crawl_test.go plan_test.go only.

verdicts.tldr: the one test showing rewritten links resolving points them at a directory the renderer never creates
verdicts.details: slug() appends a sha prefix to any argument that is not already a safe segment (crawl.go:520-533), so urlToFile("/r/x/y$file=a.gno&source") yields r/x/y/_t/file-a.gno-source-<digest>/index.html, while the fixture at crawl_test.go:127 carries file-a.gno-source with no digest. TestURLToFile:58 asserts the digest form for the same shape, so the two tests in one file disagree about what the layout is. mapURL only takes path.Dir of the fixture value (crawl.go:403), so the drift is invisible and the assertion never checks that a rewritten href lands on a directory urlToFile chose. Fix: build the pages fixture with urlToFile(u) instead of a literal.
verdicts.evidence: crawl.go:526-532 `if out == s && out != "" { return out }` then `return out + "-" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:4])`; crawl_test.go:58 wants r/gnoland/home/_t/file-home.gno-source-2ca84ba4/index.html; crawl_test.go:127 wants r/x/y/_t/file-a.gno-source/index.html.
verdicts.verify_by: compare crawl_test.go:136 with the urlToFile output asserted at crawl_test.go:67

verdicts.tldr: a per-file page with an empty name would be kept without spending a budget slot, but nothing gnoweb serves links one
verdicts.details: The asymmetry is real and read-settled: wantFile takes the budget branch for an empty name (crawl.go:227-232) and chargeFile returns true before charging when name == "" (crawl.go:243-245), so inScope admits the URL and the capture costs nothing. It has no producer in the crawled surface, though: every directory href gets a file name appended at view_directory.go:45, directory.html:48 hardcodes README.md, and the overview's license links interpolate a FileName that overview_license.go only ever sets from a matched file name. Reaching it needs a realm's own Render output to emit such an href. Fix: treat an empty file value as a per-file page in chargeFile so the two functions agree.
verdicts.evidence: crawl.go:243 `if name == "" { return true // not a per-file page }`; crawl.go:231 `return c.fileBudget[realm] < c.FileBudget`. Confirming it would need a captured page in a real crawl whose href ends `$source&file=`; grep of gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/components/views for a bare `file="` returns nothing.
verdicts.verify_by: call c.inScope and c.chargeFile on '/r/x/y$source&file=' with FileBudget=2 and no ChangedFiles; expect a charge, observe true from chargeFile with fileBudget untouched

verdicts.tldr: a gnoweb PR can hand gnodev four realms more than the cap the flag names
verdicts.details: BuildPlan truncates realms to maxRealms and records Dropped at plan.go:256-259, then appends every gnowebSeedRealms entry not already kept at plan.go:263-270, with no second bound. The triggering input is concrete: a PR touching gno.land/pkg/gnoweb plus a package imported by more than maxRealms realms, none of them the four seeds — the cap keeps 25, then all four seeds append, giving len(plan.Realms) = 29. The finder's real-tree run did not exhibit it because it changed every gnomod.toml, which makes the seeds changed realms and so already kept. Fix: append the seeds before the truncation, or re-truncate after appending.
verdicts.evidence: plan.go:256-259 `if maxRealms > 0 && len(realms) > maxRealms { plan.Dropped = len(realms) - maxRealms; realms = realms[:maxRealms] }`; plan.go:263-268 `if plan.Gnoweb { for _, r := range gnowebSeedRealms { if pkgs[r] != nil && !contains(plan.Realms, r) { plan.Realms = append(plan.Realms, r) } } }`.
verdicts.verify_by: build a fake repo whose 25 changed realms sort before gno.land/r/docs/security_patterns, set Gnoweb, and assert len(plan.Realms) <= maxRealms

verdicts.tldr: an unreadable gnomod.toml would be read as a live package, but nothing in a CI checkout makes one unreadable
verdicts.details: modFlags collapses any ReadFile error into (false, false) at plan.go:156-158, so a package whose gnomod.toml cannot be read is treated as neither draft nor ignored. LoadPkgs calls it only after ReadDir reported a gnomod.toml entry in that directory (plan.go:125, 142), so the error needs a permission change, a removal between the two calls, or a directory named gnomod.toml — none of which a fresh CI checkout produces. The mechanism is real; the loss it claims, an ignore = true package rendered and linked, has no reproducer here. Fix: return the error from modFlags and let LoadPkgs fail loudly rather than guess.
verdicts.evidence: plan.go:155-158 `func modFlags(p string) (draft, ignore bool) { b, err := os.ReadFile(p); if err != nil { return false, false }`. Confirming it would need the finder's chmod 000 run on a real examples/gno.land/r/x/<pkg>/gnomod.toml with BuildPlan observed to keep the package.
verdicts.verify_by: chmod 000 examples/gno.land/r/x/<pkg>/gnomod.toml as a non-root user, run BuildPlan on that root, observe the package present in plan.Realms

verdicts.tldr: the per-realm page cap can be changed to any value with no test going red, on a tool whose whole job is staying under an artifact size cap
verdicts.details: Every budget assertion derives its bound from the constant under test: TestCrawlerInScope and TestWantFile both set FileBudget: GnowebFileBudget, and TestWantFile's loop is `for i := range GnowebFileBudget`. The only other reference is main.go:218 returning it, so no assertion anywhere names the number 2 and the mutation to 7 leaves the suite green, as the finder observed. What survives is the mechanism (TestFileBudgetChargedOnCaptureNotDiscovery pins it with a literal FileBudget: 1), not the chosen value. Fix: assert the constant's value once, or drive the budget tests from a literal so the constant has to justify a change.
verdicts.evidence: grep -rn 'GnowebFileBudget' misc/gnopreview -> crawl.go:218 (the const), crawl_test.go:76, crawl_test.go:201, crawl_test.go:219, main.go:218. No literal 2 in any budget assertion.
verdicts.verify_by: `sed -i 's/^const GnowebFileBudget = 2/const GnowebFileBudget = 7/' misc/gnopreview/crawl.go && cd misc/gnopreview && go test ./...` — expect a failure, observe `ok`

verdicts.tldr: the link-rewriting test models a snapshot layout the writer never produces, and the collision digest round 1 asked for is absent from it
verdicts.details: slug() returns its input unchanged only when the sanitised form equals it (crawl.go:526), and "file=a.gno&source" does not survive unsafeSeg, so urlToFile appends a digest; the fixture File at crawl_test.go:127 has none, while TestURLToFile:58 asserts the digest form for the same query shape. The two disagree inside one file, and TestMapURL cannot catch it because mapURL only reads path.Dir of the fixture value. A reader checking that a rewritten href resolves to a directory the writer created is reading a directory the writer never creates. Fix: derive the fixture's File from urlToFile(u).
verdicts.verify_by: run `urlToFile("/r/x/y$file=a.gno&source")` and compare with the File literal at crawl_test.go:127

verdicts.tldr: the case reads as evidence that the snapshot's root page is handled, and no crawl can ever produce that file
verdicts.details: Seeds() walks up only while strings.Count(d, "/") >= 2 (crawl.go:95), so "/" is never seeded, and inScope refuses it on the first guard, strings.HasSuffix(base, "/") at crawl.go:191, before any realm match. Run() queues a link only when seedSet[link] || c.inScope(link) (crawl.go:148), so "/" is never captured and _root/index.html is never written; mapURL short-circuits target == "/" at crawl.go:399 ahead of the pages lookup, so even a captured root page would not be linked to. The _root branch of urlToFile (crawl.go:493-494) is therefore dead. Fix: drop the case and the _root branch, or capture "/" so both mean something.
verdicts.evidence: crawl.go:191 `if strings.HasSuffix(base, "/") { return false }` — base for "/" is "/"; crawl.go:95 `for d := path.Dir(u); strings.Count(d, "/") >= 2; d = path.Dir(d)`; crawl.go:399 `if target == "/" { return up + "index.html" + frag }` sits above the c.pages lookup at crawl.go:402.
verdicts.verify_by: assert in a test that c.inScope("/") is false and that c.mapURL("/", up) does not contain path.Dir(urlToFile("/")) even with c.pages["/"] populated
